label: JW · play
title: Jesus is the uncreated Creator (John 1:3 / Col 1:16)
text: "According to John 1:3, how many things came into existence without the Word?" (Answer: not one.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "'All' doesn't always mean all."
text: Here the verse defines it: "in the heavens and on the earth, visible and invisible, thrones, lordships" (Col 1:16). And John 1:3 says "not one thing."

label: JW · if they say
title: "He was Jehovah's master worker (Prov 8:30)."
text: Working alongside doesn't mean created. And Prov 8 personifies Wisdom (a "she"). Is God ever without wisdom?

label: JW · play
title: Jesus is Yahweh (the "First and Last" / Hebrews 1 chain)
text: "Who is the First and the Last in Isaiah 44:6?" (They'll say Jehovah.) "Does being the First and the Last mean you have a beginning?" (No.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "Jesus is the 'first and last' in a different sense."
text: "Then show me the text that makes the difference." Same title, same book, same speaker formula.

label: JW · if they say
title: "Hebrews 1:8 should say 'God is your throne.'"
text: v.8 opens "to the Son He says." The Father is speaking to the Son. And v.10 ("You, Lord…") has no throne issue at all.

label: JW · play
title: The Spirit is a Person and is Jehovah
text: "Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?" → Run the full 🔥 Holy Spirit Play. Best JW order: Acts 13:2 → Eph 4:30 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 + Acts 4:24–25. Witnesses often have no prepared answer at this point.

label: JW · play
title: Jesus is good, so He is God (Mark 10:18)
text: "Is Jesus good?" (They'll hesitate.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "He's not good like God"
text: "Name the moral flaw Jesus has that the Father doesn't."

label: JW · play
title: Watchtower prophecy test (use when they lean on the organization)
text: "Has the Watchtower ever announced a date in Jehovah's name that didn't happen?" "Have you heard of Beth Sarim, the mansion the Watchtower built in San Diego in 1929? Do you know who it was built for?"

label: JW · if they say
title: "We're not prophets, just students making calculations"
text: "Announcing future dates as God's truth is prophecy by definition."

label: JW · play
title: Only God can pay the ransom (Psalm 49)
text: "According to Psalm 49:7, can any man redeem his brother or give God a ransom for him?" (They'll say no.) This is a cumulative case. Psalm 49 does not name Jesus, and it does not prove the Trinity on its own. It says no mere man can pay the ransom and that God will redeem. The New Testament then says Jesus paid it, and calls Him God.

label: JW · if they say
title: "Psalm 49 is about imperfect men. Jesus was a perfect man, a corresponding ransom for Adam."
text: The psalm makes no exception for a perfect man. Its answer is "God will redeem." And every creature worships the Lamb for the people He purchased (Rev 5:9; Rev 5:13–14). "Would Jehovah share that worship with a creature?" (Isa 42:8)

label: JW · if they say
title: "Jehovah provided the ransom. Jesus was only the price."
text: Yes, the Father sent the Son. But the One who gave Himself is called our great God and Savior (Titus 2:13–14).

label: JW · if they say
title: "Acts 20:28 should read 'the blood of His own Son.'"
text: That verse speaks of God purchasing the church with blood. Some manuscripts read "church of the Lord," and some translations say "the blood of His own." Don't rest the case on this one verse; the chain above stands without it.

label: JW · objection
title: "John 1:1 says 'a god.' No article = indefinite."
text: A predicate noun before the verb without the article describes nature (Harner: qualitative). "The Word was God" in nature: all that God is, the Word was. "Is God 'a love'? Was John sent from 'a god'? Your NWT says 'God' in 1:6. Why not in 1:1?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Ton theon = the Almighty; theos = a lesser god."
text: That's just Greek case. Ton theon is accusative after pros; theos is nominative. Case endings aren't ranks. "Is the Father a lesser god when he's in the nominative?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Firstborn of creation" (Col 1:15) = first created
text: Prōtotokos = preeminent heir. v.16 gives the reason: "because by Him all things were created." "Who was Israel's first king? Saul. So how is David 'firstborn' of the kings?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Only-begotten" (John 3:16) = uniquely created
text: Monogenēs = the unique, only begotten Son, never "created" (Heb 11:17: Isaac wasn't Abraham's only son). "Was Isaac Abraham's only child?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Beginning of the creation of God" (Rev 3:14)
text: Archē = origin / ruler / source. He's where creation comes from. "If you're the originator of your business, aren't you its origin?"

label: JW · objection
title: "John 5:19: Jesus can do nothing on his own"
text: That shows the Persons are distinct and act together. Finish the verse: "whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise." "Does the Father do anything without the Son?"

label: JW · objection
title: "John 14:28: 'the Father is greater than I'"
text: Greater in role, in the Son's humbled human state. Not in nature. Phil 2:6–7. "Is a husband 'greater' in nature than his wife because he leads?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Psalm 8 / Heb 2: everything is subject to man, not Jesus"
text: Heb 2:9 identifies the "him": "namely Jesus." "Who are we going to trust, you or the author of Hebrews?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Daniel 7: Jesus wasn't seated / Rev 3:21: believers sit on the throne too"
text: Sharing kingdom authority ≠ sitting on high in heaven, the place that belongs to Yahweh alone (Ps 113:5). "Show me anyone other than Jesus who sits 'on high' at the right hand of the Majesty."

label: JW · objection
title: "Holy Spirit = active force"
text: → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play "Can a force be grieved?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Trinity isn't in the Bible."
text: Word–concept fallacy. "Jehovah's Witness" isn't in the Bible as a denomination name either. Is the concept taught? "Is the word 'theocracy' in the Bible?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus is Michael the Archangel."
text: Scripture never says it. Michael did not dare rebuke Satan himself (Jude 9); Jesus commands him directly (Matt 4:10). God never called any angel "My Son," and all the angels worship the Son. "To which of the angels did God ever say, 'You are My Son'?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus was raised as a spirit, not in a body."
text: He said a spirit does not have flesh and bones as He has, He showed His wounds, and He said He would raise His body. "In John 2:19–21, what did Jesus say He would raise?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Only 144,000 go to heaven."
text: Right after the 144,000, John sees a great multitude no one could count standing before the throne, serving God in His temple. "Where is the great multitude standing in Rev 7:9?"

label: JW · objection
title: "The dead are unconscious. The soul stops existing."
text: Paul expected to depart and be with Christ, away from the body and at home with the Lord. The souls under the altar speak. "How do the souls in Rev 6:10 cry out if they don't exist?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Hell isn't eternal. The wicked are simply destroyed."
text: Jesus uses the same word, "eternal," for the punishment and for the life in one sentence. "If the punishment isn't eternal, is the life?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus died on a stake, not a cross."
text: Don't make this the fight. Thomas speaks of nails, plural, in His hands, and the sign was placed above His head. Then go back to who Jesus is. "Why 'nails,' plural, for His hands?"

label: JW · objection
title: "You must use God's name, Jehovah."
text: The apostles take the Old Testament "name" texts and apply them to Jesus. Joel's "call on the name of Yahweh" becomes confessing Jesus as Lord. "In Rom 10:13, whose name is in view, given verse 9?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus is a god, a mighty one, but not the true God."
text: Jehovah says no god was formed before or after Him and He knows of no other. So is Jesus a true God or a false god? Thomas calls Him "my Lord and my God" and Jesus accepts it. "Is Jesus a true god or a false god?"

label: JW · objection
title: "People only did obeisance to Jesus, not worship."
text: All the angels worship the Son. Every creature gives the same honor to God and to the Lamb. An angel refuses it; Jesus receives it. "Why does the angel refuse what Jesus accepts?"

label: JW · objection
title: "You need Jehovah's organization to be saved."
text: Salvation is by grace through faith, not works, and not membership. When others left, Peter did not ask where to go, but to whom. "To whom did Peter say we should go?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus was a perfect man, a corresponding ransom for Adam. He didn't need to be God."
text: He had to be truly man to die in our place. But Scripture says no man can ransom another, and that God Himself redeems. The One who paid is the Word, who was God and became flesh. Run Only God can pay the ransom. "Psalm 49 says no man can pay it. So what kind of man is Jesus?"

label: JW · quick card
title: John 1:3: "not one thing came into existence without Him" → "So did Jesus create Himself?"

label: JW · quick card
title: Col 1:16–17 (NWT): "all other things." The word "other" isn't in the Greek, and the Watchtower's own interlinear shows it.

label: JW · quick card
title: Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 / 22:13: First and Last → "Does being the First and Last mean you have a beginning?"

title: Heb 1:10–12 + Ps 102:25–27: the Father addresses the Son with a Psalm spoken to Jehovah as Creator.

title: Acts 13:2 + Heb 3:7–11: the Spirit says "me / I," and the Spirit is the one tested in the wilderness → see 🔥 Holy Spirit Play.

label: JW · quick card
title: Deut 18:21–22: the 1914 / 1925 predictions → the test of a prophet.

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Holy Spirit (lead with this)
text: "Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?" → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play. Best order against Unitarians: "Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?" → Acts 13:2 → Heb 3:7–11 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 / Acts 4:25 → Rom 8:9 ("Spirit of Christ").

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Angel of Yahweh claims to be God, with no "thus says the Lord"
text: "Can we be honest with the text: does the Angel of God claim to be the God of Bethel? Yes or no?"

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Agency: a messenger speaks in the first person for the king."
text: "Show me the 'thus says the Lord.'" There isn't one. "Without it, how do you know when a messenger is speaking for God or for himself?" Moses talking in his tent and Jonah running away weren't oracles just because they had the "messenger" title.

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Can't an ambassador speak as the king?"
text: Use their analogy: "Can the agent of the King claim to BE the King?" "Yahweh can send agents, but agents can't claim to be Yahweh, or they drop dead."

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Malak means a lesser being, sent by a superior."
text: Malak / angelos names a function, not a nature. John the Baptist and his disciples are called angelos (Mark 1:2; Luke 7:24). "Does the word itself tell you what kind of being the messenger is?" "If I send you with a message, am I superior to you in nature?"

label: Unitarian · play
title: Christ is the Yahweh of the Exodus (1 Cor 8:6 → 10:9)
text: "Who's the one Lord in 1 Corinthians 8?" (They'll say Jesus.) "In Numbers 21, who did Israel test, and who sent the serpents?" (They'll say Yahweh.)

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Textual variant: some manuscripts say 'the Lord'"
text: Fine. In this same letter, the "one Lord" is Jesus Christ (8:6). Either reading lands in the same place.

label: Unitarian · play
title: Real pre-existence (John 1:3, Col 1:16, Heb 1)
text: "Do you believe that the Word was created?" (They'll say yes. Then go to John 1:3.) "According to John 1:3, was anything made without the Word? Yes or no?" "Who is the author of life according to Acts 3:15?"

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Messiah shares Yahweh's nature (Zech 13:7)
text: "In Zechariah 13:7, who is the Shepherd that gets struck?" (Jesus says it's Him, Matt 26:31.)

label: Unitarian · objection
title: The syllogism: "YHWH is the Most High; Jesus is the Son of the Most High; if Jesus is YHWH, Jesus is his own Father."
text: Equivocation. You're treating "Yahweh" as naming only one person. Scripture applies the name to the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Jesus is Yahweh, and He is not the person of the Father. "Is 'Judah' a person or a tribe?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "John 17:3: the Father is 'the only true God'"
text: Yes, the Father is the only true God. Trinitarians agree. "Only" excludes false gods, not the Son: the same John calls Jesus "the true God" (1 John 5:20). "Jude calls Jesus our 'only Lord.' Does that make the Father not Lord?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "1 Cor 8:6: one God, the Father"
text: Same verse: "one Lord, Jesus Christ." Paul splits the Shema (Deut 6:4) between Father and Son. If "one God, the Father" excludes Jesus from being God, "one Lord, Jesus" excludes the Father from being Lord. "Is the Father not Lord?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "God is not a man" (Num 23:19; Hos 11:9)
text: God is not a man by nature (who lies or changes). The Son took on a human nature (John 1:14) and stayed God. "Can the God who made human nature add it to Himself?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus died, and God can't die"
text: The Person of the Son died in His human nature. The divine nature doesn't die. Two natures, one Person. "Who was crucified in 1 Cor 2:8?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Homoousios / Nicaea / the church invented it"
text: The term is a summary of biblical teaching, not new revelation. Answer from the text, not from church history. "Fine. Set Nicaea aside. Let's just read Rev 3:14 / John 1:3."

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Archē (Rev 3:14) = first creature" / "Abba means source"
text: Archē = origin / ruler / active cause. The NT is Greek, not Hebrew, and Abba means "Father." "Does the software exist before you made it?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Context limits 'Author of life' / 'all things'"
text: Make them show the verse that limits it. "Where in the chapter does it say that?" (then wait)

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "The Spirit is rational energy / information / a vibe"
text: → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play "Can energy be rational without personhood?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus has a God (John 20:17), so He isn't God."
text: As true man He has a God. The same chapter has Thomas call Him "my God," and Hebrews calls the Son "God" while speaking of "Your God." Both are true of the one Person. "In Heb 1:8–9, who is called God, and who is His God?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus didn't know the day or the hour (Mark 13:32)."
text: Two natures. As man He grew in wisdom; as God He knows all things. "How can Peter say, 'Lord, You know all things'?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "God cannot be tempted (James 1:13), but Jesus was."
text: He was tempted as man, from outside, and never sinned. That is the point of the incarnation: a true human High Priest. "Did the temptation ever find sin in Him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "No one has ever seen God, but people saw Jesus."
text: Finish the verse: the only begotten God has explained Him. No one has seen the Father apart from the Son. And Isaiah saw Yahweh, and John says he saw Christ's glory. "Who did Isaiah see in the temple?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Philippians 2 only says Jesus didn't grasp at being equal with God."
text: He was existing in the form of God and then took the form of a slave. You cannot take on humanity if you were only ever human. "When did He 'take' the form of a slave, if He was only ever a man?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "The 'Word' in John 1 is God's plan, not a person."
text: The Word is with God, makes all things, becomes flesh, and shares glory with the Father before the world existed. Plans don't do that. "Can a plan share glory with the Father before the world existed?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "'Before Abraham was, I am' just means He was foreordained."
text: His hearers understood Him. They picked up stones. Nobody is stoned for being part of God's plan. "Why did they try to stone Him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Thomas was only exclaiming in surprise (John 20:28)."
text: The text says Thomas said it to Him, and Jesus blesses the confession instead of rebuking it. "Does Jesus correct Thomas or commend him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus is called 'god' the way judges and Moses were."
text: No judge is worshiped by angels, called Creator, or called the true God. And all are to honor the Son just as they honor the Father. "Is anyone told to honor Moses just as they honor the Father?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Matthew 28:19 was added later."
text: Every Greek manuscript that contains the passage has the three-fold name, and Paul blesses in the same three-fold way. "Which manuscript leaves it out?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "There is one mediator, 'the man Christ Jesus' (1 Tim 2:5). A sinless man was enough."
text: He is truly man; a mediator for men must be. But the next verse says He gave Himself as a ransom, and Scripture says no man can ransom another: God redeems. Hebrews says He partook of flesh and blood, and you cannot take on what you already only are. A mediator between God and men stands on both sides. "Hebrews 2:14 says He partook of flesh and blood. Who was He before He did?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Acts 13:2 → "Do actions have authority, or do persons?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Heb 3:7–11 / Ps 95 → "Who's the 'Me' the Spirit says they tested?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Gen 31:11–13 → the Angel of God says "I am the God of Bethel." "Where's the 'thus says the Lord'?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: 1 Cor 8:6 + 1 Cor 10:9 + Num 21:5–6 → "When was Christ put to the test with serpents?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: John 1:3 / Col 1:16 → "How were all things created through Him if He didn't exist yet?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 → "So Yahweh has a beginning?"

label: Mormon · play
title: No gods before Him, no gods after Him (against exaltation)
text: "Can I read you something God says about Himself and get your take?"

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "1 Cor 15:40–41: celestial / terrestrial glories."
text: In context that's about kinds of resurrection bodies, compared to the sun, moon and stars. It's about glorified bodies, not becoming creator gods.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "We're joint heirs with Christ (Rom 8:17)."
text: Yes, we inherit the kingdom. Inheriting the kingdom isn't becoming God.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "We'll be like Him (1 John 3:2)."
text: Conformed to Christ's moral image with a glorified body. Not divine in nature.

label: Mormon · play
title: God has always been God (against "God was once a man")
text: "Can we agree that God in His nature has to be infinite, always existing?" (They'll say yes.) "Joseph Smith taught God was not always God, but became God. Is that hearsay or fact?" (Use when they bring up exaltation themselves.)

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "That's not official doctrine / just my thought"
text: King Follett discourse (Joseph Smith, 1844), "God himself was once as we are now." Then: "Whether it's official or not, if a teaching contradicts the eternal God, it's a false teaching."

label: Mormon · play
title: Three separate gods vs. one God (the "Godhead")
text: "So these are three separate gods, then?"

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Jesus' baptism shows three separate beings."
text: It shows three distinct Persons. Distinct ≠ separate gods. One Being, three Persons.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Yahweh is the title of the Godhead council, like three judges sharing one court."
text: "If one judge steps out and says 'I am the court,' is that right?" But each Person is fully Yahweh, not a third of a committee. And Neh 9:6 says Yahweh alone created.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "The Angel / Son is Yahweh only by agency."
text: "Can the agent of the King claim to be the King?"

label: Mormon · play
title: Phantom prophecy (Joseph Smith wrote himself into Genesis)
text: "Where can I read the prophecy about Joseph Smith in a text that Joseph Smith didn't produce?" "Why would God pick that person to re-reveal that prophecy?" (After you name JST Genesis 50:33 and 2 Nephi 3:15.)

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Jesus read Himself into Isaiah too (Luke 4:21)"
text: "He's quoting a different prophet, from a public scroll. He didn't add new verses to Genesis."

label: Mormon · objection
title: "There was a Great Apostasy, so God restored the church through Joseph Smith."
text: Jesus promised the gates of hell would not prevail and that He'd be with His church always. "Did Jesus fail to keep His promise for 1,700 years?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Pray about the Book of Mormon and you'll feel a burning in the bosom."
text: Feelings test nothing. Scripture tells us to test by Scripture. The heart is deceitful. "If a Muslim feels a burning about the Quran, is it true too?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Ye are gods" (Ps 82:6 / John 10:34)
text: Ps 82 is about unjust human judges who "will die like men" (v.7). It's irony and judgment, not a promise of exaltation. "Do these 'gods' die?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The Father has a body of flesh and bone."
text: God is spirit, invisible, and fills heaven and earth. "Does a spirit have flesh and bones?" (Luke 24:39)

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Ezekiel 37's two sticks = Bible + Book of Mormon."
text: Read v.15–22: the sticks are Judah and Joseph/Ephraim, the divided kingdoms joined into one nation under one king. "What does v.22 say the two sticks become?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Jesus is 'a god'; the Father is 'the God.'"
text: Scripture never calls Jesus "a god." He is the God: Titus 2:13, John 20:28. "Show me 'a god' in John 1:1."

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Baptism for the dead" (1 Cor 15:29)
text: Paul says "they" (some group), not "we." It's an ad hominem for the resurrection, not a command. Heb 9:27. "Where is it ever commanded?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We are saved by grace after all we can do (2 Nephi 25:23)."
text: Scripture says grace through faith, not of works. God justifies the one who does not work but believes. Good works are the fruit, not the price. "Have you done all you can do?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The Bible is true only as far as it is translated correctly. Plain and precious things were lost."
text: God promised His word would stand forever. We have manuscripts more than a thousand years older than Joseph Smith, and none of them contain the "lost" material he added. "Which verse was lost, and which manuscript shows it?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We have a living prophet today."
text: In these last days God has spoken in His Son. Any prophet is tested by Scripture, and a different gospel is rejected even from an angel. "What happens to a prophet whose word contradicts Scripture?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Jesus and Lucifer are spirit brothers."
text: Jesus created all things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, including every angelic power. The Creator is not the brother of His creature. "If Jesus made everything invisible in heaven, who made Lucifer?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We all lived as spirits with God before we were born."
text: God forms the spirit of man within him. Only Christ is "from above." "Who does Jesus say is from above, and who is from below?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The priesthood was restored through Joseph Smith."
text: The Aaronic priesthood was set aside, and Jesus holds His priesthood permanently. Every believer is already part of a royal priesthood. "If Jesus holds it permanently, who else needs to?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Families are forever through temple marriage."
text: Jesus says that in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage. The temple veil was torn, and God does not dwell in temples made with hands. "What did Jesus say about marriage in the resurrection?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "There are three degrees of glory. Almost everyone is saved somewhere."
text: Jesus speaks of two roads and two ends: eternal punishment or eternal life. "How many destinations does Jesus name?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We're Christians too. We believe in Jesus."
text: Be gentle here. Paul warns of "another Jesus." The question is which Jesus: the eternal God who made all things, or a created spirit who became a god. "Is the Jesus you trust the eternal Creator, or a being who became a god?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "James 1:5: ask God, and He will tell you it's true."
text: James is about wisdom in trials, not a test for new scripture. The Bereans were praised for checking everything against the Scriptures. "What did the Bereans check Paul against?"

label: Muslim · play
title: THE ISLAMIC DILEMMA (run it in phases)
text: "Does the Quran say the Torah and the Gospel came from Allah? Yes or no?" The Quran says the Torah and Gospel in Christians' and Jews' hands in the 7th century were God's word and confirmed them. We have the 7th-century Bible (and far older manuscripts: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Dead Sea Scrolls). That Bible says Jesus is the Son of God, died and rose. Either the Bible is reliable, and it contradicts the Quran → Islam is false. Or the Bible is corrupted, and then the Quran confirmed a corrupted book → Islam is false. Either way, Islam fails.

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "It only confirms the original revelation, not what they had."
text: "Read it again: 'that which is with you.' Is there any part of the verse that says it's only confirming part, some, or a piece?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "It's general confirmation. It retells the stories and edits out the errors."
text: "Define 'confirm.'" (= verify as true). Then Q 2:85: "Does Allah allow people to believe some of the Scripture and reject the rest?" "Give me one verse that says the Quran only confirms part."

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Q 2:79: woe to those who write the book with their own hands."
text: That condemns people making counterfeit books. It doesn't say the real Scripture was changed. "If I wrote a book with my own hands and said it's from God, does that mean the Quran is now corrupted?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Q 5:13: they distort words from their places."
text: Distorting meaning / misquoting ≠ the text is lost. The same chapter tells them to judge by what they have (5:43, 47). And Q 6:115: "None can change His words."

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Having it is like having $100. You can still lose it."
text: The texts are present tense: they literally brought out the scroll.

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "The Bible is corrupted" (said only after a verse goes against them)
text: "You brought me the Bible as a source to prove Muhammad. When we read it, it's suddenly corrupted?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: They pivot to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity is 3 gods."
text: "You're not going to 'is Jesus God' your way out of this. Defend the Quran first."

label: Muslim · play
title: Muhammad isn't in the Bible (the John 14 and Q 61:6 claims)
text: "So where does Jesus mention Muhammad?" "So the Comforter here, you believe that's Muhammad?" (Once they cite John 14.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Only God gives eternal life
text: "Who gives eternal life?" (God.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Son vs. servant
text: "Is Jesus the son of Allah?" (They'll say no.) "Where in the Bible does it say the Son of God is just a servant?" (When they say "son" only means servant.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Tawhid consistency (the Black Stone)
text: "Can the Black Stone benefit you or harm you? Yes or no?" "Why are people rubbing oil on this rock that doesn't do anything for you?"

label: Muslim · play
title: Moral problems (only if they claim Islam is morally superior)
text: "You say Islam is morally superior. Can we read a few verses of the Quran and see?" "It talks about the women that you're allowed to have, right?" (On Q 4:24.)

label: Muslim · objection
title: "How can God be 3 and 1?"
text: Three in one sense (Persons), one in another (Being). Different categories, no contradiction. "The Quran has several transmitted readings: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun. Is that three Qurans, or one?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus never said 'I am God, worship me.'"
text: He said things only God could say, and accepted what only God receives. Watch for the goalpost shift. "First you wanted a verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' mouth?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "God is not a man" (Hosea 11:9)
text: Correct by nature. The Son added a human nature. Two natures, one Person. And don't let them skip the verse you gave first. "Do you acknowledge Heb 1:3 says the Son is the exact imprint of God's nature?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Which God sent Jesus? Who was He praying to?"
text: One God, three Persons. The Father sent the Son. Jesus prayed as a true man. "In John 17:5 Jesus asks for the glory He had with the Father before the world existed. Can a mere prophet pray that?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus wasn't crucified" (Q 4:157)
text: Every early source, Christian and non-Christian (Josephus c. AD 93, Tacitus c. AD 116), agrees He was crucified. The Quran denies it 600 years later with no source. And the Injil the Quran confirms teaches it. "Who did Allah make look like Jesus, and did he deceive the disciples into starting Christianity?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Paul corrupted Jesus' message."
text: Paul's gospel was checked and approved by Peter, James and John. And Q 61:14 praises Jesus' disciples as Allah's helpers, who won. "Q 61:14 says Allah made Jesus' followers victorious. The faith that won taught what Paul taught. Did Allah back the wrong side?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Torah is one book, but you have five."
text: The Torah = Genesis to Deuteronomy, the five books of Moses: one Torah in five scrolls. Jewish tradition says Joshua added the account of Moses' death (Deut 34). "The Quran has 114 surahs. Is it 114 books, or one?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Trinity is pagan / Allah is 'the third of three'"
text: The Quran pictures worship of God, Jesus and Mary (Q 5:116; cf. Q 5:73–75). That is not the Trinity Christians believe: one God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. "Which Christian ever taught Mary is part of the Trinity?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus ate, slept and prayed. God doesn't do that."
text: He is truly God and truly man. The Word became flesh. Hunger and sleep belong to His human nature; they don't cancel His divine nature. "If God chose to enter His creation as a man, who could stop Him?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Injil was one book given to Jesus. You have four, written by men."
text: "Gospel" means the good news about Jesus. And the Quran tells the people of the Gospel to judge by what they had in the 7th century, which was these four. "What Gospel did Christians have in Muhammad's day?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel."
text: His earthly ministry went to Israel first, as promised. Then He sent His disciples to all nations, as Isaiah foretold. "Who does Jesus send them to in Matt 28:19?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Bible has contradictions and too many versions."
text: Translations are not different Bibles. The manuscript differences are known and printed in the footnotes, and no teaching depends on them. Ask for one and read it together. "Which contradiction? Let's read it."

label: Muslim · objection
title: "God can simply forgive. He doesn't need a sacrifice."
text: A judge who lets the guilty go is unjust. God will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. At the cross He is both just and the justifier. Even the Quran ransoms Abraham's son with a great sacrifice. "If a judge lets the guilty go free, is he a just judge?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "No one can carry another person's sins (Q 6:164)."
text: The Torah the Quran confirms is built on substitution: the sins of the people laid on another. Isaiah foretold One who would bear the iniquity of us all. And Jesus is not an unwilling bystander punished for a stranger. He is the Son who laid down His life of His own accord, as the Father purposed. "What does Isaiah 53:6 say Yahweh laid on Him?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Your own Bible says each person dies for his own sin (Deut 24:16; Ezek 18:20)."
text: Deuteronomy tells human courts not to execute a son for his father's crime. Ezekiel says God holds each person to account for his own sin. Both forbid punishing an unwilling innocent. Neither forbids a willing substitute whom God Himself appoints. The same Law commands the sacrifices, and Isaiah foretells the Servant who bears the sin of many. "If substitution is forbidden, what are the sacrifices in Leviticus for?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus was only a prophet. A prophet can't redeem anyone."
text: Agreed: no mere man can. The Psalms say no man can ransom his brother, and that God Himself will redeem. That is why the Redeemer had to be God become man. Jesus said He came to give His life as a ransom. "If no man can pay the ransom, who can?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus and His disciples were Muslims."
text: His disciples worshiped Him, called Him Lord and God, and preached that He was crucified and raised. "Would a Muslim say 'My Lord and my God' to Jesus?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Muhammad is named in Song of Songs 5:16."
text: The Hebrew word there is an ordinary word for "desirable," used by a bride about her beloved. The same word family describes Ezekiel's wife (Ezek 24:16) and Israel's children (Hos 9:16). "Is Muhammad also in Ezekiel 24:16, where the same word is used?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Islam is the fastest-growing religion, so it must be true."
text: Truth isn't a headcount. Jesus said the many take the wide road. "Is something true because many people believe it?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Quran is a miracle. No one can produce a chapter like it."
text: That test has no judge and no standard. The Quran gives a better test: check with those who read the Scripture before. "Who judges the contest, and by what standard?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus said, 'Why do you call Me good? Only God is good.'"
text: He didn't say He isn't good. He asked the man why he said it. Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd. "Is Jesus good?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 5:47: "Let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 5:43: "How do they come to you for judgment while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 2:41: "Believe in what I have sent down, confirming that which is with you."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 2:85: "Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 6:115 / 18:27: "None can change His words."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: John 14:16–17: the Helper "dwells with you and will be in you." "Was Muhammad living with the disciples?"

label: Roman Catholic · play
title: Credited, not earned (justification)
text: "Do you know for sure that if you died today you'd be with God?" (Most will say "I hope so" or "No one can know." The rest of the play explains why the answer can be yes.) "What do you think makes a person right with God: what Christ did, what we do, or both?" "If God asked you, 'Why should I let you into My heaven?', what would you say?" (Listen for "I" answers: I tried, I went to Mass, I was baptized. The only answer that stands is Christ and His righteousness.)

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "'Works of the law' means only the Jewish ceremonies."
text: Rom 4:4–5 talks about any work that earns wages. Eph 2:8–9 says "not of works," and Titus 3:5 says not by "deeds which we have done in righteousness." "Are deeds done in righteousness ceremonies?"

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "We believe in grace too. The Catechism says no one can merit the first grace."
text: They will quote [CCC 2010]. Read the rest of it. The same paragraph says the justified then merit "the attainment of eternal life." Rom 11:6 says grace and works can't be mixed: "otherwise grace is no longer grace."

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Trent only condemns a dead faith, with no cooperation."
text: Read the canon they mean. Trent condemns anyone who says justification is "by faith alone… [so] that nothing else is required to co-operate" [Trent, Sess. 6, can. 9]. It also condemns justification by "the sole imputation of the justice of Christ" [can. 11]. That is exactly Rom 4:5. Sproul: if the Reformers were right, Trent anathematized the gospel.

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Faith alone means you can live however you want."
text: Saving faith comes with repentance and produces works (Eph 2:10; Titus 2:11–14; Rom 6:1–4). Works are the fruit of justification, not its cause. Trent condemns that very sentence [Sess. 6, can. 24].

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "That sounds too easy."
text: It cost Christ everything; it costs us our pride. Paul had the best religious record of anyone, and he counted all of it as loss so that he could be found in Christ with a righteousness that was not his own (Phil 3:4–9). The jailer asked what he must do, and the answer was "Believe in the Lord Jesus" (Acts 16:30–31). "What would you have to give up to come to God with empty hands?"

label: Roman Catholic · play
title: Once for all (the Mass)
text: "When Jesus said 'It is finished' on the cross, what was finished?" (John 19:30) "Is the sacrifice of the Mass a real sacrifice for sins?" (A Catholic who knows the faith will say yes [Trent, Sess. 22, can. 1, 3].)

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "It's not a new sacrifice. It's the same sacrifice made present."
text: That is what Rome says [CCC 1366–1367]. Trent still calls the Mass "propitiatory," "offered for the living and the dead, for sins" [Sess. 22, can. 3], and the Catechism says it is "offered in reparation for the sins of the living and the dead" [CCC 1414]. Heb 10:18 says that where forgiveness exists, no offering for sin remains. "If sins still need an offering, were they forgiven at the cross?"

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Malachi 1:11 predicts a pure offering among the nations."
text: In context it is the worship of God's name spreading among the Gentiles. The NT calls praise (Heb 13:15) and our bodies (Rom 12:1) sacrifices. It never calls the Supper a sacrifice for sin. (Inference from the NT pattern. The NT does not quote Mal 1:11.)

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Jesus said 'This is My body.'"
text: He also said "I am the door" (John 10:9). He said it while His body stood in front of them, holding the bread. Our church holds that the elements are representative, and that the Supper is a real communion with the risen Christ (1 Cor 10:16). See the John 6 row in the defense table.

label: Roman Catholic · play
title: One Mediator (Mary and the saints)
text: "When the disciples asked how to pray, who did Jesus tell them to talk to?" (Matt 6:9: "Our Father.") "What did Mary herself tell people to do about Jesus?" (John 2:5: "Whatever He says to you, do it.")

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "We don't worship Mary. We give her hyperdulia, not latria."
text: The distinction is Rome's, not the Bible's. Scripture doesn't grade religious service this way: Paul uses the dulia word for serving the living God (1 Thess 1:9) and for the bondage of serving "those which by nature are no gods" (Gal 4:8). Rome does teach it, and Vatican II says her role "neither takes away from nor adds anything to" Christ's [LG 62]. Then ask where Scripture teaches any category of religious honor or prayer directed to a creature. Peter and the angel refused even the bowing (Acts 10:25–26; Rev 22:8–9).

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Asking Mary to pray is like asking you to pray."
text: Scripture commands believers on earth to pray for one another (James 5:16). It never models or commands praying to the departed. It warns against seeking the dead (Deut 18:10–11; Isa 8:19). Catholics would say the saints are alive in Christ, not "the dead," so present this as an inference. Also, a creature who hears millions of silent prayers at once would need a divine attribute.

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "The Church calls her Mediatrix [CCC 969], but in a subordinate way."
text: "Is 'one mediator' in 1 Tim 2:5 a ranking, or a number?"

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Rev 5:8 shows saints offering prayers in heaven."
text: It shows the prayers of God's people presented before Him. It doesn't tell anyone to pray to the elders. Ask: "Who is the prayer addressed to?"

label: Roman Catholic · play
title: The rule that tests every rule (authority)
text: "Did Jesus ever correct religious leaders who had tradition on their side?" (Yes: Mark 7.) "If a church teaching and the Bible clearly disagreed, which one would you follow?"

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Who gave you the Bible? The Church!"
text: See the defense table. God gave it, and His people received it. The OT was Scripture before any church existed (Matt 22:31; Rom 3:2).

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Without the Magisterium, your reading is just your private opinion."
text: Everyone reads, including Catholics who read the Catechism. The question is whether Scripture is clear enough to obey (2 Tim 3:15: Timothy understood it as a child). Vatican II itself says the Magisterium "is not above the word of God, but serves it" [DV 10]. "Then can Scripture correct it?"

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "The early church fathers weren't 'Bible-only.'"
text: Cyril of Jerusalem told his catechumens: "Even to me… do not give absolute credence, unless you receive the proof… from the divine Scriptures".

label: Roman Catholic · play
title: You can know (assurance)
text: "Can a person know they have eternal life? Yes or no?" "Has a priest ever told you that you're definitely going to heaven?" (Rome says no one has absolute certainty of persevering without a special revelation [Trent, Sess. 6, can. 16; CCC 2005].)

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Claiming certainty is presumption."
text: It would be, if it rested on your performance. It rests on Christ's promise (John 6:37–40). Doubting His word is not humility.

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Mortal sin can make you lose grace [CCC 1861]."
text: True faith perseveres because God keeps it (Phil 1:6; 1 Pet 1:5; 1 John 2:19). Our church teaches that the redeemed are kept by God's power forever.

label: Roman Catholic · if they say
title: "Purgatory isn't hell. It's a purification for the saved [CCC 1030–1031]."
text: "Christ 'made purification of sins' (Heb 1:3) and His blood 'cleanses us from all sin' (1 John 1:7). What part of 'all' is left?" MacArthur: deny justification by faith alone "and you must devise an explanation" for how we reach heaven's perfection.

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "The Catholic Church gave you the Bible."
text: God gave it. His people recognized His voice (John 10:27). Jesus held people accountable to the OT before any church existed. The church received the canon; it didn't create it. "Who decided the OT canon that Jesus quoted?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Which of the 30,000+ Protestant denominations is right?"
text: The figure comes from an encyclopedia that counted thousands of "denominations" in ways that don't mean doctrinal splits, Catholic ones included. Unity is in the gospel, and Rome has its own deep internal divisions. "Do all Catholics agree on what the Catechism means?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Where was your church before Luther?"
text: Wherever God's people trusted Christ and His word. Busenitz shows justification by grace through faith in the fathers long before 1517, for example Clement of Rome: "not justified by ourselves… but by that faith". "Was the gospel missing before Trent defined it?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "James 2:24: 'justified by works and not by faith alone.'"
text: James answers the question "what kind of faith saves?" (2:14), and shows a living faith before people (2:18: "show me"). Paul answers how a sinner is declared righteous before God (Rom 4:2–5). Abraham was credited righteous in Gen 15, decades before Gen 22. "In Gen 15:6, had Abraham offered Isaac yet?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "John 6:53: 'Unless you eat My flesh.'"
text: In context, coming = eating and believing = drinking (6:35). He promises eternal life to whoever believes (6:40, 47), and He explains: "the flesh profits nothing; the words… are spirit" (6:63). The Supper hadn't been instituted yet. "Does 6:54 promise eternal life to everyone who takes Communion?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "John 20:23: priests can forgive sins."
text: Jesus sends the disciples to proclaim forgiveness, which is granted to all who repent and believe (Luke 24:47; Acts 10:43). Rome requires confession to a priest for mortal sin [CCC 1456, 1497]. No apostle ever hears a private confession and absolves. "When Peter preached in Acts 10, how did Cornelius get forgiven?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "2 Thess 2:15: hold to traditions, spoken or written."
text: The tradition Paul means is the gospel he preached in person (2:14). It was spoken or written; it wasn't a second, different body of teaching. Name one doctrine handed down orally that we can verify came from Paul. "Which of Paul's oral traditions can you name that isn't in Scripture?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "1 Tim 3:15: the church is the pillar and support of the truth."
text: The context is a local church's conduct, with elders and deacons (3:1–14). A pillar holds up the truth; it doesn't create it. The truth it holds up is Christ (3:16). "Does a pillar make the roof, or hold it up?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Matt 16:18: Peter is the rock and the first pope."
text: Rome teaches this [CCC 881–882]. But Peter calls Christ the stone (1 Pet 2:4–8), and Paul says no foundation can be laid except Christ (1 Cor 3:11). The keys and binding go to all the disciples (Matt 18:18). Nothing in the text says anything about successors or Rome. "Where does the passage mention a successor?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "The pope is infallible when he speaks ex cathedra."
text: Vatican I defined it [Pastor Aeternus, ch. 4]. Yet Peter himself was publicly rebuked for compromising the gospel (Gal 2:11–14). At the Jerusalem council, James gave the judgment (Acts 15:13–21). Peter called himself a "fellow elder" (1 Pet 5:1). "If Peter could be wrong on the gospel, can his successor?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary was conceived without sin (Immaculate Conception)."
text: Defined in 1854 [CCC 491]. Mary calls God "my Savior" (Luke 1:47). She offered the sin offering after childbirth (Luke 2:22–24; Lev 12:6–8), and Scripture says all have sinned. No text exempts her. "Why would a sinless woman need a Savior and a sin offering?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary was ever-virgin."
text: Rome teaches it [CCC 499–500, 510]. Joseph "kept her a virgin until she gave birth" (Matt 1:25). The Gospels name Jesus' brothers and mention sisters, with His mother (Matt 13:55–56; Mark 6:3; Acts 1:14). Rome reads these as relatives [CCC 500]. The plain sense is siblings. "If 'brothers' with 'His mother' means cousins here, how would Mark have said brothers?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary was assumed body and soul into heaven."
text: It was defined as dogma in 1950 [Munificentissimus Deus 44]. Scripture says nothing about it. Binding a doctrine with no biblical witness is the very authority question again. "What verse would you give a new believer for this?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Purgatory: 1 Cor 3:15, 'saved, yet so as through fire.'"
text: That passage is about testing a minister's work (3:10–14), not purging a person's sins. To be absent from the body is to be at home with the Lord (2 Cor 5:8). The thief went to paradise today (Luke 23:43). Rome also cites 2 Macc 12:43–45 [CCC 1032], which isn't Scripture (see below). "In 1 Cor 3, what gets burned: the man's sins or his work?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Indulgences can reduce temporal punishment, even for the dead."
text: Rome teaches this [CCC 1471, 1479, 1498]. Christ "made purification of sins" (Heb 1:3), and the gift of God isn't obtained by works or payments (Acts 8:20; Isa 55:1). Indulgences assume a debt that Christ left unpaid. Rome says they draw on a "treasury" that includes the prayers and good works of Mary and the saints [CCC 1476–1477]. Scripture knows no one with righteousness to spare: when we have done everything, we are still unworthy slaves (Luke 17:10). "Did Christ pay all of it, or only part?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Baptism regenerates (John 3:5; Acts 2:38; 1 Pet 3:21)."
text: Rome teaches justification is conferred in baptism [CCC 1992, 1213, 1263]. But Cornelius received the Spirit before baptism (Acts 10:44–48), and the thief was saved without it. Peter says it is "not the removal of dirt… but an appeal to God" (1 Pet 3:21). Spurgeon: "Baptism without faith saves no one". "If baptism saves, why does Paul say Christ didn't send him to baptize?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "You removed seven books (the Apocrypha)."
text: Trent declared them canonical [Sess. 4]. The OT was entrusted to the Jews (Rom 3:2), and they never received these books. Jesus framed Scripture as Law, Prophets and Psalms (Luke 24:44). The NT never quotes them as Scripture. "Did Israel ever receive 2 Maccabees as Scripture?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Sola Scriptura isn't in the Bible."
text: Scripture is the only revelation called God-breathed (2 Tim 3:16). Jesus judged tradition by it (Mark 7:13), and Isaiah sends us "to the law and to the testimony" (Isa 8:20). Busenitz traces this conviction through the fathers: Athanasius said "the sacred and inspired Scriptures are sufficient". "What else does Scripture call God-breathed?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "We need priests and sacraments; grace flows through the Church."
text: Rome holds that the sacraments are necessary for salvation [CCC 1129]. Christ holds His priesthood permanently (Heb 7:23–25), the veil is torn (Matt 27:51), and every believer is a priest (1 Pet 2:9). "Who does Hebrews say we can approach God through?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Catholics and evangelicals believe the same gospel now."
text: Trent's canons on justification have never been revoked, and they are quoted in the current Catechism (CCC 1992 echoes Trent). MacArthur: "nothing has changed since Trent". Being kind doesn't mean treating the difference as minor. "Has Rome withdrawn Trent's anathema on faith alone?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary is the Mother of God."
text: Rome teaches this [CCC 495]. The One she bore is truly God (Luke 1:35, 43), but she is mother to His humanity. His deity has no mother and no beginning (John 1:1; Mic 5:2). Scripture's own name for her is "the mother of Jesus." The title is used to lift her up; Mary used her own words to lift Him up. "What does Mary call God in Luke 1:47?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary is the Queen of Heaven."
text: Rome says she was exalted "as Queen over all things" [CCC 966]. Scripture uses "queen of heaven" only for a false goddess whose worship God judged (Jer 7:18; 44:17–19, 25). A Catholic will say that is a different figure, and it is. The point is that Scripture never gives Mary a throne. She calls herself the Lord's slave, and in heaven every creature worships God and the Lamb. "In Revelation 4 and 5, who is on the throne, and who is worshiped?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary cooperated in our redemption, and graces come to us through her."
text: MacArthur calls Co-Redemptrix "unofficial reality" in Rome even though it was never made dogma, and he calls the idea blasphemous. In 2025 the Vatican's doctrine office said the title is not appropriate [Mater Populi Fidelis]. The teaching did not change. The Catechism still says she cooperated "in the Savior's work" and still calls her Advocate, Helper, Benefactress and Mediatrix [CCC 968–969], and John Paul II used the title Co-Redemptrix himself. If they say "the Church dropped that," ask which paragraph of the Catechism was removed. None was. (The word "Co-Redemptrix" is not in the Catechism, so quote 968–969, not the title.) Scripture: there is no savior besides God, and our High Priest is not hard to reach. "If the title is wrong, why does the Catechism still call her Mediatrix?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Mary has appeared: Guadalupe, Lourdes, Fatima."
text: Rome itself says no one is bound to believe private revelations [CCC 67]. Scripture tells us to test every spirit. A sign or vision that turns prayer and trust toward anyone but God fails the test, whoever seems to bring it. Mary is never seen again in Scripture after Acts 1:14. "If even an angel from heaven can't change the gospel, can an apparition?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "The rosary: 'pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death.'"
text: The Hail Mary entrusts the hour of death to her care [CCC 2677], and the five decades have 53 Hail Marys to 6 Our Fathers. In Scripture the dying man calls on the Lord, and He hears. Jesus told us to pray to the Father, to ask in His own name, and not to pile up repeated words. "In Psalm 116, who does the dying man call on?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Statues and images only remind us of the person, like a family photo."
text: Rome teaches that honor given to an image passes to the one it shows [CCC 2132]. The commandment forbids the bowing, not only the making. The Psalms say those who trust in images become like them, and Isaiah speaks of those who "pray to a god who cannot save." See the icons play. "Does the commandment forbid only making images, or also bowing to them?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "We adore Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament."
text: Rome teaches the consecrated host is to be given the worship due to God [CCC 1378; Trent, Sess. 13, can. 6]. If the bread is still bread, that is worship given to a created thing. Christ's body is in heaven, where He sat down and waits until He returns. This was the point the English martyrs died for. "According to Acts 3:21, where is Christ's body now?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "The pope is the Vicar of Christ and head of the Church."
text: Rome teaches this [CCC 882]. Scripture gives the headship to Christ alone. The One Jesus sent to stand in His place is the Holy Spirit. "Holy Father" is what Jesus calls the Father. Peter calls himself a fellow elder and tells elders not to lord it over the flock. "In John 17:11, who does Jesus call 'Holy Father'?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Peter was the first bishop of Rome, and the popes succeed him."
text: Scripture never shows it. Paul writes to Rome and greets two dozen people with no mention of Peter, and says he does not build on another man's foundation. Peter was sent to the circumcised. This is an argument from silence, so say so. But even if Peter died in Rome, no text passes his office on. "Strengthen your brothers" and "Tend My sheep" restore a man who had denied Him, and Peter gives the same charge to every elder. The earliest writings connected with Rome (1 Clement, Ignatius's letter to the Romans, the Shepherd of Hermas) speak of elders who lead the church and name no single ruling bishop there. Augustine took the rock of Matt 16:18 to be Christ, whom Peter confessed. "Why doesn't Paul greet Peter in Romans 16?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "Priests must be celibate."
text: Rome treats this as a discipline, not a doctrine: its Eastern-rite priests may be married [CCC 1579–1580]. Scripture's overseers are normally married men, Peter had a wife, and Paul warns about those who forbid marriage. Singleness is a gift to some, not a rule for an office. "In 1 Timothy 3:2, what does Paul expect of an overseer?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "We're saved through faith, baptism and keeping the commandments."
text: That is Rome's own wording: salvation "through faith, Baptism and the observance of the Commandments" [CCC 2068, quoting Vatican II]. If they say the works are done by grace [CCC 2008], it changes nothing: grace plus works is still not grace (Rom 11:6). In Acts 15 some said faith was not enough without circumcision and the Law of Moses. Peter answered that God cleanses hearts by faith and that we are saved "through the grace of the Lord Jesus." Paul says that if you add a requirement to be justified, Christ will be of no benefit to you. "At the Jerusalem council, which side did Peter take?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "We believe in grace, faith and Scripture too."
text: Rome uses all three words. It says each one is necessary. The disagreement is whether each one is enough. Is Scripture enough to equip the man of God, or must tradition be added? Is faith enough to justify, or must works be added? Is Christ's one offering enough, or must it be offered again? "Necessary, or enough? Which word would you use for what Christ did?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "The Church has taught the same faith for 2,000 years."
text: Compare two of Rome's own documents. In 1302 Pope Boniface VIII defined that it is "absolutely necessary for salvation" for every human being to be subject to the Roman Pontiff [Unam Sanctam]. Today's Catechism says the plan of salvation includes Muslims, and that people who do not know the gospel through no fault of their own can be saved [CCC 841, 847]. Rome's answer is that doctrine "develops." That is Cardinal Newman's argument from 1845, and it admits that the teaching has not stayed the same. Scripture speaks of a faith delivered once for all. "If both statements are official teaching, which one do I follow?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "It's the same Jesus. Does the rest really matter?" / "Are you saying Catholics aren't Christians?"
text: Say it plainly and with love: Rome teaches a different gospel. Paul's opponents in Galatia believed in Jesus, His cross and His resurrection, and added one requirement. He called it a different gospel, put it under God's curse, said those who receive it are "severed from Christ," and warned that a little leaven leavens the whole lump. MacArthur: Roman Catholicism is "false Christianity teaching a false gospel," and "people need to be rescued from this system." Busenitz: unless Rome's false doctrines are rejected, there is no hope of salvation in that system. A person is saved only by turning from every other trust to Christ alone, and a person who has done that cannot stay at peace with what Rome teaches. "I'm not asking which church you belong to. What are you trusting to make you right with God?"

label: Roman Catholic · objection
title: "My family would never forgive me if I left."
text: Take this seriously; it is often the real obstacle. In Jesus' day people believed and stayed silent because confessing Him meant being put out of the synagogue. He never hid the cost, and He promised that no one who leaves family for His sake will lose by it. You may not need to tell them to leave anything today. Ask them to settle first who they are trusting. "If it were true, would you want to know, even if it cost you?"

label: Roman Catholic · quick card
title: Rom 4:4–5: "Does God justify the one who works, or the one who believes?"

label: Roman Catholic · quick card
title: Heb 10:14, 18: "If His one offering perfected us for all time, and there's no longer any offering for sin, what is offered at Mass?"

label: Roman Catholic · quick card
title: 1 Tim 2:5: "How many mediators between God and men does Paul name?"

label: Roman Catholic · quick card
title: Mark 7:8–13: "Can a religious tradition ever cancel out God's word?"

label: Roman Catholic · quick card
title: 1 John 5:13: "John wrote so you can know you have eternal life. Do you?"

label: Roman Catholic · quick card
title: Gal 1:8–9: "If even an apostle or an angel can't change the gospel, can a council?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · play
title: Their own test of tradition (Philaret Q23)
text: "Would you agree that we must only follow tradition that agrees with Scripture?" (Their own catechism says so: "We must follow that tradition which agrees with the divine revelation and with holy Scripture" [Philaret Q23].) "If an old tradition and a clear verse disagreed, which would win?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Only the Church can interpret Scripture [Dositheus, Decree 2]."
text: Then Philaret's test can never fail, because the Church grades its own test. Cyril of Jerusalem (an Eastern father) told his hearers not to believe even him "unless you receive the proof… from the divine Scriptures," and Basil said hearers should examine teachers, "receiving what is in conformity with the Scriptures and rejecting what is opposed to them".

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Basil said unwritten tradition has the same force [quoted in Philaret Q24]."
text: Basil said both. Ask: "Which of the two lets you correct an error if one creeps in?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "1 Tim 3:15: the Church is the pillar of truth."
text: See the defense table.

label: Eastern Orthodox · play
title: Justified now (against salvation as a lifelong process)
text: "Can a person be declared righteous by God today, completely, and know it?" "Your church's manual says justification 'is not a single, once-for-all event' [OCA EOCB, p. 218]. Can we look at what Paul says?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Faith working through love (Gal 5:6), so faith and works [Dositheus 13]."
text: Gal 5:6 describes what living faith does. The same letter says we're justified "by faith in Christ and not by the works of the Law" (Gal 2:16), and condemns adding anything (Gal 3:1–3).

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Salvation is healing and union, not a legal transaction."
text: Scripture uses both: a verdict (Rom 8:33–34) and new life (2 Cor 5:17). We agree on union and transformation (2 Cor 3:18). We don't let healing replace the verdict.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Faith alone is easy believism."
text: No. Saving faith repents and submits to Christ as Lord (Luke 13:3; Rom 10:9). Works are fruit, not a co-cause.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Isn't that the Protestant reading? The fathers taught synergy."
text: Busenitz collects patristic witnesses to justification by faith, e.g., Clement of Rome: "not justified by ourselves… but by that faith". Letham notes some honored Orthodox writers who sound the same note.

label: Eastern Orthodox · play
title: Icons and the second commandment
text: "Does the second commandment forbid only making images, or also bowing down to them?" (Ex 20:5) "When Israel made the golden calf, who did Aaron say they were worshiping?" (Ex 32:4–5: a "feast to Yahweh.")

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "We give icons veneration, not worship (latria); the honor passes to the prototype [Nicaea II; CCC 2132 says the same]."
text: That is their position. The commandment forbids the bowing, not just a wrong inner attitude. Schooping, a former Orthodox priest, asks how mere "veneration" of an image becomes worship of Christ: if it doesn't, it's too little for Christ; if it does, it's worship given through an image.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "God commanded cherubim in the tabernacle (Ex 25:18)."
text: Yes, images can exist. But no one was ever told to bow to, kiss or pray before them, and the bronze serpent shows what happens when they do (2 Kings 18:4).

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "The Incarnation made God visible, so we can picture Him."
text: God made Himself visible in Christ (John 14:9). Ortlund documents that early Christians did not bow to images, and that icon veneration came later; he notes that Epiphanius opposed it in the 4th century.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Nicaea II anathematizes people who refuse to venerate icons."
text: It does: "If anyone does not salute such representations… let him be anathema" [Nicaea II, anathemas]. Ask gently: "Was every Christian before 787 who didn't kiss icons under a curse?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · play
title: He bore our sins (penal substitution)
text: "In Isaiah 53, whose iniquity did Yahweh lay on the Servant?" "Was Jesus punished in our place, or only defeating death for us?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "That makes the Father a vengeful pagan god punishing a 'whipping boy' [OCA EOCB, pp. 186–88]."
text: We reject that caricature too. Father and Son act together in love (John 10:17–18; Rom 8:32; 1 John 4:10). The OCA manual itself affirms that justification "stands alongside others" as a biblical metaphor [EOCB p. 188]. This isn't a conciliar dogma for them, so ask what this person believes.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "It's Anselm's medieval theory."
text: Isaiah 53 is seven centuries before Christ. Schooping, a former Orthodox priest, shows a substitutionary reading in Chrysostom and Theophylact.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "The East teaches Christus Victor."
text: So does Scripture (Col 2:15; Heb 2:14–15). But Col 2:14 says the victory came by canceling "the certificate of debt" against us. Both are true together.

label: Eastern Orthodox · play
title: Dead, not just sick (ancestral sin)
text: "Before God made us alive, how does Paul describe us: sick or dead?" (Eph 2:1) "Do you believe we inherit only death from Adam, or also guilt?" (The OCA says "only Adam and Eve are guilty of that sin" [OCA Q&A, "Original Sin"].)

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "That's Augustine. The East never accepted original guilt."
text: Paul wrote Rom 5 centuries before Augustine. Also note that the Confession of Dositheus says infants "are subject to original sin" and need its remission [Decree 16], so Orthodox sources themselves aren't unanimous.

label: Eastern Orthodox · if they say
title: "Then infants who die go to hell?"
text: Our hope rests in God's mercy and character (2 Sam 12:23). It doesn't rest on denying what Rom 5 says about Adam.

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Sola Scriptura is a 16th-century invention."
text: The fathers treated Scripture as the final court, including Eastern fathers. Athanasius: "the sacred and inspired Scriptures are sufficient to declare the truth." Cyril of Jerusalem: don't believe even me without proof from Scripture. "Were Athanasius and Cyril Protestants?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "The Church is the pillar and ground of the truth (1 Tim 3:15)."
text: Philaret uses this verse [Q18]. The context is a local congregation with elders and deacons. A pillar holds up the truth; it doesn't author it. "Does a pillar make the truth or hold it up?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Hold the traditions, by word or letter (2 Thess 2:15)."
text: Philaret quotes this verse to say tradition must agree with Scripture [Q23]. Paul's tradition is the gospel (2:14), not a separate source. "Your catechism says tradition must agree with Scripture. So which one tests the other?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "We are the one true Church; you split off."
text: The Church is all who are united to Christ by faith (Eph 2:19–22). Our church holds that each local church is self-governing under Christ. Schooping, from the inside, calls Orthodox ecclesiology "inextricably exclusive". "Is someone who trusts Christ alone, outside your communion, in Christ?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "We have apostolic succession from the apostles."
text: Apostles had to be eyewitnesses of the risen Christ (Acts 1:21–22); the foundation was laid once (Eph 2:20). The succession Paul commands is of teaching (2 Tim 2:2). He warned that men in the succession would rise up teaching error (Acts 20:29–30). "Can a bishop in succession teach error?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Theosis: 'God became man so man might become god.'"
text: Ask what they mean first. They do not mean sharing God's essence (they distinguish essence and energies). We agree on union with Christ and glorification (Rom 8:29–30; 1 John 3:2). We differ on making it a cooperative process that grounds acceptance with God. "Is theosis the ground of your acceptance with God, or the fruit of it?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Salvation is synergy: God and I working together."
text: Philaret: a right faith "and good works" are necessary "to save one's own soul" [Q3]. Scripture says God gives the faith and raises the dead (Eph 2:5, 8–9; John 6:44). We work out what He has worked in (Phil 2:12–13). "In Phil 2:13, who is doing the working?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Icons have always been part of the Church."
text: Ortlund documents that early Christians did not bow to or kiss images, and that 4th-century voices like Epiphanius opposed it. Veneration was defined in 787 [Nicaea II]. "Can you show icon veneration in the New Testament?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Mary is the Theotokos."
text: The title means "God-bearer," and it was first used to guard a truth we hold: the One she bore is truly God (Luke 1:35, 43). But she is mother to His humanity. His deity has no mother and no beginning (John 1:1; Mic 5:2). Scripture's own name for her is "the mother of Jesus" (Acts 1:14). We part ways where the title is used to lift her up, pray to her, or call her ever-virgin. "Do you mean she bore the One who is God, or that she shares in His glory?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Mary is ever-virgin."
text: Philaret teaches it [Q186]. Matt 1:25 says "until she gave birth," and the Gospels name His brothers alongside His mother (Matt 13:55–56; Mark 6:3). Orthodox usually explain these as Joseph's children from an earlier marriage. The plain sense is siblings. "What would Mark write if he meant siblings?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Asking the saints to pray is like asking a friend."
text: The OCA manual says this, and adds that the saints help and heal "themselves" too [EOCB p. 72]. Scripture models asking the living (James 5:16), never the departed, and gives us direct access through Christ (Heb 4:16; 7:25). Busenitz notes how such practices developed historically, citing Calvin's Treatise on Relics. "Who does Hebrews tell you to approach for help in time of need?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Baptism saves (John 3:5; 1 Pet 3:21)."
text: Dositheus: without baptism "none is able to be saved" [Decree 16]. But the Spirit came on Cornelius before baptism (Acts 10:44–48), and Peter says baptism saves "not [as] the removal of dirt… but an appeal to God." Spurgeon: "Baptism without faith saves no one." "Was the thief on the cross saved?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "The Eucharist is truly His body and blood."
text: Dositheus affirms a change of substance [Decree 17]. Our church holds that the elements represent Christ's body and blood, and that the Supper is a real communion with the risen Christ (1 Cor 10:16). Jesus' words are spirit (John 6:63), and His sacrifice is not repeated (Heb 10:14, 18). "Does the Supper proclaim His death, or offer it again?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "God isn't angry. Sin is sickness, not crime."
text: Sin is both disease and guilt. Scripture speaks of wrath (Rom 1:18; John 3:36) and of a verdict (Rom 5:18). The OCA manual itself keeps "justification (our acquittal)" as a biblical theme [EOCB p. 188]. "Does John 3:36 say the wrath 'abides' or 'heals'?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "We don't inherit guilt, only death."
text: The OCA says so [Q&A, "Original Sin"]. Rom 5:18–19 says one man's disobedience brought "condemnation to all men" and "made" many sinners. Dositheus speaks of infants' "original sin" [Decree 16]. "What does 'condemnation to all men' mean?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Our church is 2,000 years old; yours is 500."
text: The test is whether a church holds the apostles' teaching (Acts 2:42; Gal 1:8). Age doesn't settle it: the Pharisees' traditions were old too (Mark 7:13). Busenitz shows Scripture-alone convictions in the early church. "If a 2,000-year-old church taught error, how would anyone know?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "The Divine Liturgy is ancient and beautiful. Protestant worship is shallow."
text: Shallow worship anywhere is a fault, but age and beauty do not make worship true. Justin Martyr (c. 150) describes the early service as reading the apostles and prophets, preaching, prayer, and the Supper. Letham's concern is that Orthodoxy downplays preaching. Tozer: God tired of rituals that pointed ahead; Christ fulfilled them. "What did the earliest services you can document center on?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Toll houses / the soul's journey after death."
text: Toll houses are not dogma, even in ROCOR, which declined to define them in 1980. Don't argue it as if it were their official teaching. Scripture: to be absent from the body is to be at home with the Lord (2 Cor 5:8; Luke 23:43). "Is that a teaching you're bound to, or a pious opinion?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "God is known in His energies, not His essence. Theology is experience, not propositions."
text: Keep it short. God truly reveals Himself in His word, and we can know Him truly, though not exhaustively (John 17:3; 1 Tim 6:16). Letham's concern is that Palamas's framework can lead to agnosticism about God. Then bring it back to the gospel. "Can God tell us true things about Himself in words?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "We pray for the departed, and our prayers help them."
text: The Confession of Dositheus says that some who repented without bearing fruit go to Hades and are delivered by "the prayers of the priests" and the good works of their relatives [Decree 18]. They will say it is not purgatory. It is still a second chance after death, and Scripture gives none. Scripture teaches that death is followed by judgment, that a great chasm is fixed, and that the believer who leaves the body is at home with the Lord. It never shows a prayer changing anyone's state after death. "If today is the day of salvation, what are we telling people who plan to be prayed out later?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "Our infants are baptized, chrismated and given communion."
text: That is their practice: baptized and chrismated infants receive communion [OCA, The Orthodox Faith, vol. 2]. It follows from believing that baptism gives new birth (see the baptism row). In Scripture those who "received his word" were baptized and then shared in the breaking of bread, and each person is told to examine himself before he eats. Our church baptizes believers, by immersion, and the Supper is for those who profess faith. "Can an infant examine himself?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · objection
title: "I'd lose my family and my people if I left the Church."
text: For many cradle Orthodox, church, family and nation are one thing, so this is the real obstacle. Don't wave it away. Jesus never hid the cost and promised that no one who leaves family for His sake will lose by it. Ask them to settle first who they are trusting. "If it were true, would you want to know, even if it cost you?"

title: 2 Tim 3:16–17: "If Scripture equips the man of God for every good work, what's still missing?"

title: Mark 7:8–13: "Can a tradition that's very old still cancel God's word?"

title: Ex 20:4–5: "Does the command forbid only making images, or also bowing to them?"

label: Eastern Orthodox · quick card
title: Isa 53:5–6, 10: "Who laid our iniquity on the Servant, and who was pleased to crush Him?"

title: Rom 5:1: "'Having been justified': is that finished or still in progress?"
